So I love jazz, everything about it sounds so different than anything I've heard before. But unfortunately, I live in an area where Jazz is seen as "snooty" music so no one listens to it, therefore I've never heard a lot of artists. I've listened to lots of random jazz piano on YouTube, and some Miles Davis. Other than that I haven't heard much and was wondering who are your favorite artists? Don't worry, I'll listen to Coltrane next

I have a couple of suggestions for more contemporary groups. The first is Kamasi Washington and his new album The Epic. It's essentialky a 3 disc album that comes in at around 3 hours so I would take it in chunks unless you are on a road trip. It has a nice combo jazz band feel at times with only some saxes, a piano, and drum kit. Then he whips out the string section for some symphonic moments. The solos are pretty good and tend to hover on the post-modern/free jazz side of things rather than a virtuosic solo but they are still good.

The second group is Snarky Puppy and its a big jazz band that records in a studio and is definitely has a more traditional jazz band feel to them. Their latest album had them play with some orchestra I think so it has a larger and more grandiose feel to it.

Thanks! I was going to listen to Kamasi on my flight to/from Seattle but unfortunately I could only find one song on his new album on spotify... I'll definitely check them out though

Edit: it looks like The Epic is on spotify now, Thanks for reminding me

No problem. The Epic is in my running for top ten albums of the year and it's great if you are into some longer more intricate jazz.

I've only heard a few snarky puppy songs but one of my friends whose opinion I respect loves them so I'd say give them a listen.

Other than that try out some big band artists like Glenn Miller, Bennie Goodman, or Artie Share. They have more of a swing and upbeat feel.
